To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we propose a new sparse attention mechanism, called routing attention, (ii) we demonstrate that routing attention can be efficiently implemented in a single matrix-multiplication layer, and (iii) we show that routing attention is a powerful and flexible building block that enables the construction of efficient transformers for various sequence modeling tasks.
• The proposed Sparse Routing Transformers (SRT) achieve state-of-the-art results on the GLUE benchmark, surpassing BERT, RoBERTa, and ELECTRA.

(i) routing transformers are a new class of sparse transformers that can achieve competitive performance with significantly fewer parameters than full self-attention, (ii) routing transformers can be trained with standard self-attention losses, (iii) routing transformers can also be applied to cross-modal tasks, and (iv) routing transformers can improve the performance of existing models, such as BERT, by replacing their full self-attention with routing transformers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of an efficient and accurate sparse attention mechanism for transformer models.
the design of efficient sparse self-attention mechanisms for transformer models.
a new approach for learning sparse self-attentions in a data-dependent manner.
